topic: Second terminal development milestones (FSRU + onshore infrastructure)
wiki_text: Singapore's second LNG terminal will pair an offshore FSRU with new onshore connecting infrastructure at Jurong Port. In October 2024 SLNG signed agreements with Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), Jurong Port, and Wood (FEED) to develop the project; MOL will own, manage and operate the FSRU under a long-term time charter once delivered, while SLNG operates the terminal facility itself. The FSRU (204,000 cbm storage, 5 mtpa regasification capacity, built to run up to 25 years without drydocking) is under construction at Hanwha Ocean's Geoje shipyard in South Korea for about US$413 million, with the keel laid 26 May 2026 and delivery expected by October 2027. SLNG awarded the onshore connecting-infrastructure EPC contract (main process area, FSRU jetty, pipelines to the national gas grid) to China Communications Construction Company (Singapore) in November 2025, with groundbreaking in late March 2026. The FSRU is planned to be moored at Jurong Port and connected to Singapore's gas network by 2030, taking SLNG's combined throughput capacity (with the existing Jurong Island terminal) to up to 15 mtpa.

topic: New LNG truck-loading facility (does not change import capacity)
wiki_text: SLNG began construction of a new LNG truck-loading facility at Jurong Island (China International Water & Electric Corp. (S) Pte. Ltd., EPC contractor), targeted for completion in 2026, to support growing domestic trucked-LNG distribution. The facility has two loading bays and accommodates larger 40-footer trucks (vs. the existing facility's 20-footer limit). It is administratively part of the SLNG Terminal site but segregated from the main marine-import operations, and does not change the terminal's nameplate import capacity (reported elsewhere as 9 mtpa average / 11 mtpa peak).

source_urls.title: Singapore Starts Building New Loading Facility for Trucked LNG

wiki_text: In July 2026, Singapore LNG signed a terminal-use agreement with a unit of Chinese utility Jiaxing Gas, allowing Jiaxing Gas to use SLNG's terminal facilities. Deal specifics (capacity, duration) were behind a paywall and could not be confirmed.

source_urls.title: Singapore LNG, Jiaxing Gas seal LNG terminal use deal
